blocks.text: Welcome to the EatOuts blog
If you're reading this, you already know EatOuts. It's the app where you find Botswana's best restaurants, see today's promos, and order in WhatsApp. No account. No commission. No nonsense.
This blog is where we go deeper. Behind-the-scenes stories, guides to the food you didn't know was on your doorstep, and honest breakdowns of what it actually takes to run a restaurant in Botswana.
What you'll find here

items: Guides — Weekend in Maun. Best chisanyama in Gaborone. Where to eat when it's 3pm and you've forgotten lunch.
Stories — the people behind the plates. The chefs, owners, and dishes that make Botswana's food scene worth showing up for.
Updates — new venues, new features, new reasons to open the app.

blocks.text: We won't post every day. We'll post when we have something worth saying. When we do, you can find it here, or search a #tag if you're looking for something specific.
EatOuts is built in Botswana, for Botswana. Every restaurant on the app keeps 100% of their sales. **We take no commission, ever.**

posts.title: Why we don't take commission (and never will)
posts.subtitle: The rule we built the whole app around

blocks.text: Why we don't take commission
The rule we built the whole app around
Every food delivery app in the world takes a cut. 15%, 20%, sometimes 30% of every order goes to the platform. The restaurant keeps the rest. That's the model.

We don't do that. EatOuts charges restaurants a flat monthly subscription and takes zero percent of every order. If a restaurant sells P10,000 worth of food through EatOuts in a month, they keep P10,000. We don't see any of it.
Commission is a tax on restaurants that can least afford it.
blocks.attribution: — every restaurant owner we've ever spoken to

blocks.text: Why it matters

items: Restaurants keep their margins. A 20% commission is the entire profit margin for most small venues.
Prices stay honest. When platforms take a cut, restaurants bake it into the menu. You pay more.
The incentive is right. We only make money if the restaurant is on the app. They only pay us if the app is useful.

blocks.text: How we make money
P300 onboarding fee, then P100–P500 per month depending on the tier. That's it. That's the whole business model. No data sales, no ads, no commission.
If you run a restaurant in Botswana and want to be on EatOuts, WhatsApp us. We onboard new venues every week.

blocks.text: Friday nights at The Yellow Giraffe
Why it's the Friday spot

Tshukudu Road, just off the main drag in Gaborone. A courtyard, string lights, and coffee that turns into cocktails at exactly 5pm. The Yellow Giraffe has been quietly turning Friday evenings into something worth leaving the house for.

blocks.alt: The Yellow Giraffe courtyard at dusk
blocks.caption: The courtyard, just before the Friday rush

blocks.text: The happy hour runs 17:30 to 19:30 every Thursday and Friday. Cocktails, wine, beer, and liquor all drop in price. The espresso martini is the one to order.
What to order

items: Long Neck Island — a cocktail that lands somewhere between a mojito and something stronger
The mixed grill platter — if you're eating dinner, this is the one
Salted caramel latte — for the person who's driving

blocks.text: **Happy hour: 17:30–19:30, Thursdays and Fridays.** Walk-ins welcome. Book via WhatsApp for groups of 6 or more.

blocks.text: Masa Poetry Nights: what you missed, and what's next
One stage. Countless voices.

On the last Thursday of every month, a room in central Gaborone fills with the sound of people saying things out loud. Poetry, spoken word, live music. Masa Poetry Nights, run by Think Tanks Advertising, has become the platform Botswana's poets deserve — and one of the best nights out in the city.
One stage. Countless voices.

The September edition, themed "Celebrating Botswana Through Words", ran until 00:30. Twenty-three artists. Meredith Ms B, Phodiso Modirwa, Thekalatswene, and a dozen more. Tickets were P100 early bird, P150 at the door, P50 for students.

posts.subtitle: Value, not cheap

blocks.text: The 5 best-value dishes in Gaborone right now
Value, not cheap
"Value" isn't the same as "cheap". A P50 dish that leaves you hungry is worse value than a P120 dish you'll think about for a week. These five are the ones we keep going back to.
1. The TYG Taco Bowl — The Yellow Giraffe
Fresh salsa, guacamole, couscous with feta, cheddar, lettuce, and crunchy Doritos. Choose chicken, beef sirloin, or lean mince. P95–P120. You will not be hungry after this.
2. The half chicken and chips — any chisanyama worth its salt
Botswana does one thing better than anywhere else on earth, and it's grilled half chicken. The best versions are the ones with no menu — just ask what's on the fire. Expect P70–P100.
3. The Giraffe Tower Double Cheese — The Yellow Giraffe
Two beef patties, double cheese, lettuce, tomato, house sauce, chips. P100. It's not subtle. It's not supposed to be.
4. Chicken Prego Roll — any Spur
Grilled chicken breast on a Portuguese roll with caramelised onions and peri-peri. P109.90. Sometimes you just want something that works.
5. The Full Vegetarian Breakfast — The Yellow Giraffe
Two eggs, grilled halloumi, roasted tomatoes, baked beans, sautéed spinach, toast. P75. If you've never had halloumi for breakfast, this is the one to convert you.
Every dish above is available on the EatOuts app. Tap a venue to see the full menu.

posts.subtitle: The feature nobody asked for and everybody needs

blocks.text: How to split the bill without the drama
The feature nobody asked for and everybody needs
You've been there. Eight people, one bill, everyone arguing about who had the ribs and who only had a salad. EatOuts has a feature for that. Here's how it works.
Step one — build your order
Open a restaurant, tap menu items, add to cart. Each venue has its own cart, so nothing gets mixed up.
Step two — tap "Split the Bill"
This opens a screen where you add names — one per person at the table. You can add as many as you want.
Step three — assign each item
For every item in the cart, decide who's paying for it. If two of you shared the wings, tap +1 for each person. Everything stays editable until you're done.
Step four — send it
Tap "Send the full bill to the restaurant" and the whole order goes to the venue's WhatsApp. Or send each person their own share — the app opens your WhatsApp contacts and pre-fills the message.
**Pro tip** — the app includes the restaurant's WhatsApp number at the bottom of every split message, so if someone needs to forward their share, they can.

blocks.text: Botswana's chisanyama culture
A beginner's guide

Every Motswana knows what a chisanyama is. If you're visiting, the first thing to understand is that it's not really a restaurant. It's not really a bar. It's a place where meat, fire, and people happen to be in the same spot.

blocks.caption: The fire does most of the work

blocks.text: What it is

Chisanyama literally means "place of cooking meat" in Setswana. In practice, it's an open-air venue with one or more braai stands, a butchery attached or nearby, and a bar. You pick your cut, they grill it, you sit outside and eat it.
What to order

items: Seswaa — slow-cooked, pounded beef. The Botswana national dish.
Beef short rib — the cut most often on the fire.
Chicken (half or quarter) — always grilled over open flame, never fried.
Pap or palichi — the starch. Never optional.
Chakalaka — a spicy vegetable relish that comes on the side.

blocks.text: How to behave
Don't rush. Chisanyamas run on their own clock. Order a drink, sit down, and let the meat take its time. Nobody is going to bring you a menu; you ask what's on the fire.
Chisanyama is not a restaurant you go to. It's a place you end up staying at.
Where to go in Gaborone
Start with the ones on the EatOuts app. Ed-La's Chisanyama, Kwa Ga Ncinci Restaurant, and The Braai Place are three good entry points.

blocks.text: A weekend in Maun
Where to eat, from Friday night to Sunday lunch
Most people come to Maun for the Delta. But the town has a food scene that deserves its own trip. Here's a weekend itinerary that doesn't require a 4x4 or a bush pilot's licence.
Friday night — Marc's Eatery
Italian-Botswana fusion, done with real care. The pasta is fresh, the portions are generous, and it's one of the few places in Maun that treats dinner as an occasion. Book ahead on weekends.
Saturday breakfast — Hilary's
The kind of café that makes you want to move to Maun permanently. Fresh juice, honest coffee, and a breakfast menu that does both the healthy and the indulgent well. Sit outside if you can.
Saturday lunch — Tandurei Indian Restaurant
Maun's answer to the Indian craving. Butter chicken, fresh naan, and a menu that understands spice levels. The Moteti Road branch is the original.
Saturday afternoon — Okavango Craft Brewery

Botswana's first craft brewery. The Delta Lager is the one to order — golden, cold, brewed with water from the Delta. Tour the brewery if you can. It's a small operation and the staff are proud of what they've built.
Saturday dinner — The Eden Kitchen
International menu, well-executed. Whatever the special is, order it. The kitchen knows what it's doing.
Sunday — The Duck Cafe Bar
Late breakfast, slow coffee, no rush. The kind of Sunday you deserve before driving back to Gaborone.
Every venue above is on the EatOuts app. Tap through to see full menus, photos, and contact details.

blocks.text: How we onboard a restaurant in one afternoon
The whole concierge process, start to finish
One of the first things people ask us is "do I have to fill in a form?". The answer is no. Here's what actually happens when a restaurant joins EatOuts.
12:00 — the first WhatsApp
The owner sends us a message. Name of the restaurant, town, and the WhatsApp number they want orders to go to. That's the whole brief.
12:30 — we visit or call
If they're in Gaborone, we visit. If not, we do a 20-minute call. We ask about the menu, the signature dishes, and what makes the place different. We take photos of the food and the room.
14:00 — we build the listing
While the coffee's still warm, we build the whole page: identity, location, hours, menu with prices, three or four photos. No forms for the owner to fill in. No dashboard for them to learn.
15:30 — the first promo
Every new venue gets one free promo to feature in the daily feed. It could be a signature dish, a happy hour, a weekly special. We write the copy, they approve it.
16:00 — the preview
We send them a private link so they can see exactly what diners will see. They tell us what to change. We change it. Two rounds, maximum.
17:00 — live
Once the P300 setup fee is confirmed, the listing goes live. Their first diner can order that evening.
Our goal is one afternoon. We've done it in 90 minutes for a small café and in two days for a multi-location restaurant. Either way, the owner never touches a dashboard.
